help.howitworks.switching_service_source.backTranslation: Why the choices change: a source that fails permanently, a service that is disabled, that becomes unavailable, out of quota or that is not included in your plan, or a download that has finished leave the lists or are shown as unavailable. Switching back and forth does not, by itself, remove a choice.

Progress: when choosing a source would mean throwing away progress already made, DebridPulse first asks Discard downloaded progress?. A service change that would mean throwing away progress is instead refused, with the reason would discard downloaded data; switch its source to confirm.

With a download paused: choosing another source for a file that had already started downloading is accepted and saved, but nothing starts. The service and source shown remain the current ones and, next to the service name, a message indicates where the file will go, for example Switch to Real-Debrid (rapidgator.net) on resume. Choosing again replaces that choice; choosing the source already in use removes it. After resuming, it shows Switching to … until the switch takes effect and then disappears. If a download's paused files go to different places, or if the destination is not known, no destination is shown. A file that never started has nothing to carry over, so the new source simply applies when it starts. Choosing a service with the download paused works as described above, except that the download stays paused: a service that can accept the link in use takes over immediately (the badge shows it), and one that must first prepare a copy shows Preparing … and only takes over after resuming. These messages appear on the Download activity and Downloads rows; both kinds can appear at the same time.

It is on by default for AllDebrid, Debrid-Link, Premiumize and Real-Debrid, and off by default for TorBox, whose torrent limits are tighter. While it is on, that service also adds torrents that another service is delivering, so as to be ready to take over if needed, and, when you switch a download to another service, the torrent that this service had already started is kept as a backup instead of being removed. This uses that account's torrent slots and limits; a new download that needs a slot reclaims it first. Turn it off to reserve that service's slots for its own downloads: its backups are then removed. A choice you have already saved is kept.

help.settings.users_access.user_accounts.backTranslation: User accounts lists each person with their role, the way they sign in and whether the account is enabled. Add local account creates an account with a username and password. A role changed in Edit user applies immediately: that person's open pages reload with the new role, without ending the session. Each person has a DebridPulse username, distinct from the display name: an OIDC account receives it on first sign-in, and it is the name used to sign in with a local password; the pencil beside it in the Edit user title changes it and keeps any saved password. Click an account's name to see its details and activity, where a pending request can be withdrawn individually. Disable and Remove first show how many pending download requests the account has; those requests are withdrawn, a transfer that someone else also requested continues, and completed downloads are never affected. Disabling also ends the account's sessions and disables its tokens; removing keeps the account's history and deletes its own notification settings. A removed OIDC sign-in that comes back receives a new account, which stays disabled until it is enabled. Merge joins two or more accounts into the account you choose to keep; two accounts that share a verified e-mail are flagged, but only a merge joins them. DebridPulse always keeps at least one usable Admin, and you cannot change your own role or disable your own account.

Select a backup and use Save backup (download a copy), Restore backup or Remove; Add backup uploads a saved copy after verifying it. Restoring pauses processing, creates a safety backup of the current state, re-verifies the chosen backup, replaces the current database and settings, and restarts DebridPulse's services.
